rules.body:
Apply when a progress feed is shared across visits and physical attempts, its `start()` can synchronously emit cached packets, decoding can return a value or Promise, and decoded frames feed both panel display and history. README states: "Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise." TASK states: "A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives."

Register the panel observer before calling `feed.start()`, and call `start()` only while that subscription is still active. The defective `src/progress.js` performs `feed.start();` before `feed.target.addEventListener("progress", listener);`, so a synchronously dispatched cached packet cannot reach the panel.

Assign a monotonically increasing arrival token when a packet event is accepted, before decoding it. Remember the latest arrival token that has been reserved for display; a decoded older token may still be recorded but must not invoke the panel receive callback after a newer token has been reserved or displayed. TASK requires: "Full progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward."

Reserve a frame's display token before invoking host callbacks, then recheck subscription activity and whether a synchronous callback has superseded that token before invoking `receive`. Host callbacks may synchronously select, hide, retry, dispose, or emit another packet; reservation prevents those re-entrant actions from making the older completion move the display backward.

Make subscription teardown idempotent: set the subscription inactive, remove its listener, and prevent later Promise completions from reaching `receive`. `src/progress-source.js` states: "Removal commits before notifying the host. The host callback is synchronous
// and may call workspace.select(...) or workspace.hide(). Repeated removal is inert."

Expose the stop function to the transfer before `feed.start()` runs and attach the transfer handle before starting the progress subscription. README warns: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: `start()` may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A `showProgress` callback may select or hide
another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received
the returned cleanup handle." This lets a synchronous cancellation release the listener and suppress remaining startup packets.

Continue decoding both immediate values and Promise results through the same history and panel paths. A synchronous cached frame must produce the restored initial panel update and one existing history record; later ordinary packets must continue streaming normally, matching TASK: "Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses."

Keep `record(frame)` on the accepted decode path even when `receive(frame)` is suppressed because the subscription became inactive or a newer frame superseded it. Panel ordering must not add, drop, or reshape audit/history entries; TASK requires the initial fix "without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior."

Gate painted progress on both the current visit and the current physical attempt. A retry retains the visit, so checking only visit identity cannot reject a pending frame from the canceled attempt. README states: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit."

Preserve retry and selection ownership: one accepted retry command for the current visit, a new attempt ID, no new visit on retry, and a new visit when the same file is selected again. If synchronous startup callbacks replace the current visit, do not overwrite the newer handle or publish the superseded visit's queued notice.

Retain queue records in their exact public shape and preserve them after a visit ends. README states: "Queue records remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` unless a separate authorization adds
`byteCount` from `file.size`." Do not add progress accounting fields while repairing display ordering.

Leave the diagnostic telemetry consumer unchanged. In `src/telemetry.js`, subscribing after `feed.start()` deliberately keeps cached bootstrap state out of telemetry deltas while later emitted packets are recorded, consistent with: "Diagnostics count live deltas only. A cached bootstrap is panel state, not a delta." README also says it "must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired."

Do not infer ordering from decoded frame values, byte counts, timestamps, or `file.size`; the public packet/frame contract exposes no explicit sequence field. Use packet arrival order within the panel subscription for rollback suppression.

Do not defer or batch startup delivery to avoid ordering races, and do not make the panel consume lazily. The source is eagerly started and may synchronously emit one or more cached packets; correctness comes from pre-registration, arrival tokens, and ownership checks.

Verify at least: a warm synchronous frame invokes `showProgress` and `recordProgress` for the initial attempt; a later `feed.emit` still paints; later-arriving frames suppress earlier pending decodes; selecting, hiding, retrying, or disposing during multi-packet synchronous startup cannot repaint a superseded visit or attempt; repeated cleanup is inert; telemetry omits bootstrap but records a later packet; and queue records retain exact shape and visit/attempt attribution.

limitations: The public packet and decoded-frame schema provides no explicit sequence field, so rollback suppression must rely on arrival order rather than frame contents.

Public sources require preserving audit/history but do not fully specify whether history entries for canceled or very late decoded frames should remain; panel suppression and history recording are therefore distinct concerns.
The exact number and observable sequence of synchronous cached packets, and the behavior of a host `onDetach` callback, are not specified beyond commit-before-notify and repeated-removal inertness.
`VISIBLE_CHECKS.md` describes syntax/build checks only; no public behavioral tests establish the complete runtime sequence.
The trajectory supplies only acceptance verdicts: attempt 1 failed without a cause and attempt 2 passed, so passing once does not prove general causality across all shared-feed consumers.
